component.name: google-functions
component.title: Google Cloud Functions
component.description: Manage and call functions in Google Cloud Functions.
component.label: cloud

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

CamelGoogleCloudFunctionsOperation.description: The operation to perform, which overrides the operation option.

CamelGoogleCloudFunctionsEntryPoint.description: The name of the function in the source code that runs when the new function is called, such as the exported function for Node.js or the fully qualified class name for Java. createFunction requires it, unless pojoRequest=true.

CamelGoogleCloudFunctionsRuntime.description: The runtime ID of the new function, for example nodejs20, python312 or java17. createFunction requires it, unless pojoRequest=true. Google lists the supported runtime IDs in the Cloud Functions documentation.

CamelGoogleCloudFunctionsSourceArchiveUr.description: The Cloud Storage URL, starting with gs://, of the ZIP archive that holds the source code of the new function. createFunction requires it, unless pojoRequest=true, and creates the function with an HTTPS trigger.

CamelGoogleCloudFunctionsResponseObject.description: The full response of the service: the CallFunctionResponse for callFunction, the GenerateDownloadUrlResponse for generateDownloadUrl, or the GenerateUploadUrlResponse for generateUploadUrl. The message body holds only the result or the signed URL.

producerIn.description: The data to call the function with, for callFunction (the default): text is sent as it is; bytes, a stream, a file, XML (a DOM Node or a Source), an enum or a character are converted to text; and a Map, a List or another POJO is marshalled to JSON with a plain Jackson ObjectMapper, so marshal a POJO that needs custom JSON, such as one with java.time fields, yourself. No body fails, as the data is required. The other operations take their input from options and headers. With pojoRequest=true the request object of the operation, such as a CallFunctionRequest

producerOut.description: The result of the function as text for callFunction, with the whole CallFunctionResponse in the CamelGoogleCloudFunctionsResponseObject header: a response with an error, of a function that failed, fails the exchange with a CamelExchangeException. By the operation: a List of CloudFunction for listFunctions, the CloudFunction for getFunction, createFunction and updateFunction, Empty for deleteFunction and the signed URL as text for the URL operations

functionName.label: common
functionName.description: The name of the function, without the projects/{project}/locations/{location}/functions/ prefix. The producer builds the full name from it and the project and location options. Not used by listFunctions and generateUploadUrl, and not used when pojoRequest=true.

serviceAccountKey.label: common
serviceAccountKey.description: The service account key file (JSON) used to create the CloudFunctionsServiceClient. It is loaded as a resource with the classpath:, file:, http: or https: prefix, and a value without a prefix is read from the classpath. When not set, the Application Default Credentials are used, for example from the GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS environment variable. Not used when the client option is set.

location.label: producer
location.description: The region of the functions, for example us-central1. Every operation needs it, unless pojoRequest=true, where the request object names the location.

operation.label: producer
operation.description: The operation that the producer performs with the Cloud Functions v1 API. When not set, callFunction is used, which Google allows only for limited traffic, such as tests. The CamelGoogleCloudFunctionsOperation header overrides this option. updateFunction works only with pojoRequest=true.

pojoRequest.description: Whether the message body is the request object of the Google Cloud SDK for the operation, which is sent as it is: a ListFunctionsRequest, a CloudFunctionName for getFunction, a CallFunctionRequest, a GenerateDownloadUrlRequest, a GenerateUploadUrlRequest, a CreateFunctionRequest, an UpdateFunctionRequest or a DeleteFunctionRequest. The project, location and functionName options and the createFunction headers are then not used.

project.label: producer
project.description: The ID of the Google Cloud project that holds the functions. Every operation needs it, unless pojoRequest=true, where the request object names the project.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer,advanced
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

client.label: advanced
client.description: The CloudFunctionsServiceClient to use for the calls. When not set, a single CloudFunctionsServiceClient in the registry is used, otherwise the endpoint creates one with the serviceAccountKey or the Application Default Credentials and closes it when it stops. A client that is set or autowired is not closed by the endpoint.
